blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (E-mail address and display name written to the application log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: log.info("new signup email=%s name=%s id=%s", email, display_name, user_id)
findings.recommendation: Log only the opaque id (`log.info("new signup id=%s", user_id)`). As written, every call to `signup("ada@example.org", "Ada")` writes the member's e-mail address and display name to the application log, where they escape the members table's retention and erasure (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 17 erasure) and reach whoever or whatever reads or ships the logs.
findings.title: E-mail address and display name written to the application log

findings.recommendation: Drop `email` from the event properties and send only `user_id` (or no identifier at all, since the proposal only needs sign-ups to be counted). As written, each sign-up posts the member's e-mail address to https://beacon.example.com/v1/events (app/analytics.py:5,9), a third-party processor, although the stated purpose — "Sign-ups are counted in product analytics" — does not need it (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c), Art. 25). The copy at Beacon is also out of reach of the member's access and erasure rights (Art. 15, 17).
findings.title: E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS

findings.evidence: """Product analytics, sent to the Beacon SaaS (beacon.example.com)."""
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the change introduces Beacon as a processor receiving member data (at least `user_id`), but the proposal's Impact and Domains sections do not name it. State whether a processor agreement exists (GDPR Art. 28), where Beacon processes the data (Chapter V transfers outside the EEA) and add it to the record of processing (Art. 30). Could not be verified from the repository.
findings.title: Beacon is a new processor not identified in the plan

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — collects e-mail addresses and display names
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the proposal says the change collects e-mail addresses and display names but states neither their lawful basis (GDPR Art. 6), nor how long the member record is kept, nor how it is deleted, backups included (Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). Only the controller can tell what was decided; record it in the proposal.
findings.title: Purpose, lawful basis and retention of the sign-up data not stated
